description: Represent large ring or disk scenes as co-moving patches in Hill coordinates and only instantiate high-fidelity particles near the camera or selected body. The bridge is between planetary-ring local models and game-engine chunk streaming: physics lives in local frames while the UI still feels like one world.
mathematical_formalization: For patch p centered at R_p, evolve local states under Hill equations: x_ddot - 2 Omega y_dot - 3 Omega^2 x = f_x, y_ddot + 2 Omega x_dot = f_y, z_ddot + Omega_z^2 z = f_z; remap bodies when ||x_local|| > L_p / 2
analogical_connections: Open-world terrain chunks become co-moving orbital patches.
Weather tiles around a camera map onto local Hill frames around an orbit.
A rolling-window signal processor inspires local physics windows with stitched global summaries.
implementation_hypothesis: Maintain a patch manager around the active region; evolve each patch with a shearing-sheet integrator; represent distant patches by aggregate moments for rendering and weak forcing; hand bodies across patch boundaries with coordinate transforms instead of global reinitialization.
experiment_seed: Simulate a narrow ring and an asteroid belt with a moving camera; compare memory, runtime, and trajectory continuity against a single global-coordinate implementation.

novelty_claim: The new element is to reinterpret shearing-sheet locality as a streaming architecture, making a large interactive world feasible with minimal local physics.
differentiation: Research shearing-sheet codes usually study one local box at a time. This concept uses many transient local boxes as a runtime system, driven by visibility and interaction rather than by a fixed scientific domain.
